498.summary: The class explores Joshua's leadership and his typological representation of Jesus Christ, emphasizing the importance of divine guidance and the fulfillment of God's promises. It highlights the significance of Joshua's name and his role in leading the Israelites into the Promised Land, drawing parallels to Jesus' role in salvation.

499.summary: The class explores Rahab's faith and transformation from a harlot in Jericho to an ancestress of Jesus Christ. It emphasizes the power of faith in God's salvation and the inclusion of Gentiles in God's plan.

500.summary: The class explores Joshua 1-7, focusing on the crossing of the Jordan River and the conquest of Jericho as types of Christ's future reign. It emphasizes the faith of Rahab and the divine leadership of Joshua, highlighting the themes of God's judgment on the wicked and the establishment of His kingdom.

501.summary: The class discusses Joshua 1-7, focusing on the symbolism of the twelve stones taken from the Jordan River, emphasizing God's ability to raise up children to Abraham beyond mere physical lineage. It explores the concept of divine fatherhood and the contrast between human and divine character, culminating in the significance of Christ's atonement and resurrection.

502.summary: The class discusses the significance of circumcision in Joshua 5, emphasizing Joshua's role and the symbolism of circumcision as representation and the removal of reproach. It draws parallels to Christ's sacrifice, highlighting the concept of representation and the removal of sin through faith in Christ.

503.summary: The class discusses the fall of Jericho in Joshua 6, interpreting it as a type of the future judgment of God on the nations. It emphasizes the role of God's people in executing divine judgment and the importance of aligning one's emotions with God's attitude towards the wicked world.

504.summary: The class discusses Achan's sin in Joshua 7, emphasizing the collective responsibility of the ecclesia and the consequences of greed and disobedience. It also explores the themes of repentance, judgment, and the hope of redemption through Christ's return.
